item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.18420v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Atomic disorder offers a potent degree of freedom to tailor material properties, yet the resulting vast configuration space obscures structure-property relations and hinders rational inverse design. Here we introduce Graph Amorphous Diffusion Transformer (GaDiT), a generative model that combines dynamic periodic graphs, masked conditioning and an interval-weighted training-noise distribution. GaDiT generates high-quality disordered structures while accelerating sampling by two orders of magnitude compared with existing corrector-based approaches, as demonstrated across two-dimensional amorphous carbon and three-dimensional amorphous silicon and silica. Moreover, GaDiT supports conditional generation under single or combined structural features, physical properties and preparation conditions in a unified model, and enables inverse design that expands accessible structure-property ranges beyond the training distribution. To interpret these structures and the trained network, we propose a conditioned atomic response mapping analysis, revealing both the global structural descriptors and the local atomic environments that govern target properties. Overall, GaDiT establishes a general framework for interpretable generation, inverse design and structure-property discovery for disordered atomic structures.

item.title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy
item.description: arXiv:2611.18430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) show promise for predicting materials properties, but interpretability remains a challenge, particularly understanding whether attributed feature importance reflects physical reality or statistical art…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.18430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) show promise for predicting materials properties, but interpretability remains a challenge, particularly understanding whether attributed feature importance reflects physical reality or statistical artifacts. Here, we present a methods validation study that deliberately overfits a physics-aware GNN ensemble to probe the robustness of feature-ranking approaches. Using the CoMoFeNiCu high-entropy alloy system with three stoichiometries, we train GNNs to predict decomposition enthalpies from DFT-calculated structures while explicitly constraining output weights to encode feature importance. By design, our dataset is limited (approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways) to control compositional complexity and enable precise interrogation of local chemistry effects. We validate that feature rankings capture meaningful local-environment information through a series of atomic swap perturbations: perturbing individual atomic sites and re-ranking features reveals spatial decay consistent with the GNN's interaction cutoff, confirming that weights encode neighbor-shell effects rather than global stoichiometric artifacts alone. Results demonstrate that feature attribution methods can remain physically interpretable even under overfitting, provided validation is rigorous. This work establishes a foundation for trustworthy interpretability in materials GNNs and sets the stage for scaling to multiple chemistries and testing generalization across compositional spaces.

item.title: Connecting finite-size scaling and renormalization-group flows in Anderson localization on random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.31872v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the relation between two complementary descriptions of the Anderson transition on small-world random graphs: finite-size scaling of eigenfunction moments and renormalization-group (RG) flows of multifractal dimens…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2609.31872v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the relation between two complementary descriptions of the Anderson transition on small-world random graphs: finite-size scaling of eigenfunction moments and renormalization-group (RG) flows of multifractal dimensions $D_q$. The RG flows recover the qualitative structure previously reported for the information dimension $D_1$, while their extension to other $D_q$ with smaller moment orders $q<1/2$ confirms the strongly multifractal nature of the localized phase characterized by a clear distinction between multifractal and localized scaling behaviors of different moments within the localized phase. On the other hand, we show that we can construct another beta function characterizing the flow of eigenfunction moments, whose collapse onto a single function across different disorder strengths supports single-parameter scaling of the normalized moments within each sector. These results raise an interesting question about the interpretation of two-parameter scaling: while a two-dimensional flow structure has been inferred from the information dimension $D_1$ alone, our analysis reveals two distinct scaling sectors by considering different eigenfunction moments. To characterize these properties, one should consider different observables, such as large $q>1/2$ and small $q<1/2$ eigenfunction moments, which are associated with distinct critical behaviors, in particular different critical exponents.

item.title: Dynamical confinement creates quasi-critical scale-free dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2602.00374v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Scale-free avalanches are commonly interpreted as signatures of criticality. Conventional theoretical frameworks predict robust avalanche-size exponents $\tau$ bounded by $3/2$, while dissipation is expected to drive syste…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2602.00374v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Scale-free avalanches are commonly interpreted as signatures of criticality. Conventional theoretical frameworks predict robust avalanche-size exponents $\tau$ bounded by $3/2$, while dissipation is expected to drive systems away from criticality, by progressively suppressing large events. Yet earthquakes and numerous dissipative experiments exhibit scale-free dynamics with non-universal exponents $\tau > 3/2$, challenging both expectations. Using the Olami-Feder-Christensen model as a minimal theoretical framework, we identify two fundamentally distinct routes to scale-free dynamics:a genuinely critical scenario, in which avalanches continuously explore the entire system and remain permanently capable of spanning it; and a quasi-critical scenario, in which dissipation and the traces left by past avalanches generate dynamical confinement. Rather than remaining at a critical point, the system explores a power-law distribution of distances to criticality. We show, using a simple analytical model, how this mechanism produces scale-free avalanche statistics with dissipation-dependent exponents exceeding $\tau = 3/2$. Our results establish a physical mechanism for scale-free dynamics beyond conventional criticality, providing a framework for understanding the non-universal avalanche statistics observed in earthquakes and dissipative systems.

item.title: Thermalization Across Scales on a Digital Quantum Processor
item.description: arXiv:2603.12236v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Thermalization of isolated quantum many-body systems normally unfolds via dynamical spreading of entanglement across progressively increasing spatial scales. The speed of this dynamical process, however, can be affected by…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2603.12236v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Thermalization of isolated quantum many-body systems normally unfolds via dynamical spreading of entanglement across progressively increasing spatial scales. The speed of this dynamical process, however, can be affected by the presence of local disorder. Here we study the crossover between slow and fast thermalization in a disordered two-dimensional Heisenberg Floquet model using digital quantum simulations with up to 100 superconducting qubits. Our experiment measures subsystem purities and $Z$-basis marginal collision entropies for patches of up to $3\times 3$ qubits. We resolve the onset of thermalization across scales by tracking each quantity's approach to its asymptotic value. In regimes where the system is moderately entangled, we validate our calibrated quantum simulations against state-of-the-art classical simulations. Near the crossover to fast thermalization, the classical methods no longer reliably converge due to volume-law growth of entanglement. By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.

item.title: Consensus in Effective Model Inference for Disordered Ising Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.10731v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When independent learners are trained on data from the same disordered system, finite and noisy samples can lead them to different descriptions of the underlying physics. We quantify the reproducibility of such description…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2609.10731v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When independent learners are trained on data from the same disordered system, finite and noisy samples can lead them to different descriptions of the underlying physics. We quantify the reproducibility of such descriptions through consensus, the degree of agreement among independently trained models. In a teacher-student framework on the two-dimensional random-bond Ising model, an ensemble of students each infers a single uniform effective coupling from a finite set of equilibrium configurations drawn from one quenched bond realization. Aggregating the inferred couplings across students and realizations yields the consensus distribution, whose width quantifies the agreement among learners. The variance of this distribution separates exactly into a finite-sampling contribution, bounded below by inverse of Fisher information, and a quenched-disorder contribution. Sum of these two variance is minimized near critical region, so the consensus width has a minimum near the pseudocritical temperature that sharpens with increasing disorder. The two minima arise from different mechanisms: the sampling term inherits the critical peak of the Fisher information, while the disorder term is temperature-independent at leading order and acquires its critical minimum only at fourth order in the disorder strength, through the covariance between the linear and cubic responses to the bond disorder. Because the students fit a uniform coupling to a heterogeneous lattice, the inferred coupling also carries a misspecification bias that survives in the infinite-data limit. This bias displaces the minimum of the mean-squared error above the consensus minimum, so the temperature at which independent learners agree most closely is not the temperature at which their shared answer is most faithful.

item.title: Quantum violation of Causal Friendliness in the instrumental scenario
item.description: arXiv:2611.17431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How far can quantum theory depart from a classical worldview? Bell inequality violations show that no theory can simultaneously uphold absoluteness of observed events, freedom of choice, relativistic causality, and classical causal …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How far can quantum theory depart from a classical worldview? Bell inequality violations show that no theory can simultaneously uphold absoluteness of observed events, freedom of choice, relativistic causality, and classical causal explanations. While generalized notions of causality, capable of incorporating quantum resources, can account for Bell correlations, the Local Friendliness theorem showed that, in extended Wigner's friend scenarios, the conflict between quantum theory and causal explanations persists even after classical causality is abandoned. This revealed a new form of nonclassicality stronger than what was revealed by Bell's theorem. However, Local Friendliness has been confined to Bell causal structures so far, and it remains unknown whether a related form of nonclassicality persists in more general causal networks. Here we answer this question by considering a Wigner's friend version of the instrumental network, a paradigmatic causal structure in which communication between parties is allowed, and, unlike the Bell scenario, relativistic causality does not impose any restriction. We show, both theoretically and in a proof-of-principle photonic experiment, that quantum correlations are incompatible with Causal Friendliness, which is the conjunction of the absoluteness of observed events and the generalized nonclassical causal constraints imposed by the network. Such constraints extend relativistic causality from Bell scenarios to networks of arbitrary structure. These results establish a form of quantum nonclassicality stronger than previously observed in instrumental-network violations of classical causality, generalizing Local Friendliness beyond Bell-Wigner scenarios and uncovering a new class of correlations with potential applications in future quantum technologies.

item.title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $\Omega(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

item.title: Optically-induced electric Aharonov-Bohm effect
item.description: arXiv:2611.17435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although it was proposed almost 70 years ago, the electric version of the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect, where the interference pattern of quantum charged particles is affected by electric fields that do not interact locally with them, …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although it was proposed almost 70 years ago, the electric version of the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect, where the interference pattern of quantum charged particles is affected by electric fields that do not interact locally with them, was never experimentally implemented. Here we propose a feasible way to experimentally verify such an important effect, for an electron double-slit interferometer with the slits carved in a nonlinear crystal. The AB phase is generated by a quasi-DC electric field induced in the crystal with the passage of a light pulse (the optical rectification effect) while the electron is superposed in the two slits. We show that this procedure can change the interference pattern of a ensemble of electrons even if they are subjected to negligible electric fields during their propagation, considering feasible parameters.

item.title: QuantumInputOutput.jl: A Julia framework for input-output theory with quantum pulses and the SLH formalism
item.description: arXiv:2611.17451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interaction of traveling photonic pulses with quantum systems is a fundamental process for many quantum technologies such as quantum communication, control, and measurement protocols. The so-called SLH formalism, named for the t…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interaction of traveling photonic pulses with quantum systems is a fundamental process for many quantum technologies such as quantum communication, control, and measurement protocols. The so-called SLH formalism, named for the triple of operators that parametrize the dynamics, in combination with virtual emission and absorption cavities provides a general toolbox to describe such processes. However, modeling open quantum systems driven by propagating quantum pulses becomes cumbersome once several components, channels, and temporal modes are involved. Here we present QuantumInputOutput.jl, an open-source framework that automates this derivation process: first, symbolic expressions for the Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators are derived using predefined SLH rules and symbolic quantum algebra. Next, the obtained operators are converted to (time-dependent) numerical matrices or are used to obtain higher-order mean-field equations. The numerical expressions are presented in a form immediately suitable for solving the time evolution of the master equation and analyzing the output modes via correlation functions. Besides its usefulness for numerical simulations, the framework also provides a convenient tool to derive symbolic expressions for one-dimensional quantum systems such as multilevel emitters in cavities or waveguides.

item.title: Efficient quantum-circuit simulation of classical control of computational order
item.description: arXiv:2611.17454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that quantum circuits with classical control of computational order admit an efficient simulation by fixed-order quantum circuits: any such transformation acting on $N$ independent quantum channels can be deterministically, …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that quantum circuits with classical control of computational order admit an efficient simulation by fixed-order quantum circuits: any such transformation acting on $N$ independent quantum channels can be deterministically, exactly, and universally simulated using at most $N^2$ queries. We generalize these constructions to extended, bipartite quantum channels and quantum instruments, and demonstrate that they can be implemented catalytically, without consuming the additional $N^2-N$ queries required for the simulation. In the case of quantum circuits with quantum control of computational order, we prove a similar simulation result, but restricted to unitary input channels (hence non-universal). These results show the limitations of the computational power of these classes of transformations in the studied scenarios.

item.title: The radical pair mechanism can generate nuclear-spin entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2611.17497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The radical pair mechanism is a quantum-mechanical process underlying weak magnetic field effects in chemical and biological systems. While nuclear polarization and electronic entanglement in this mechanism have been studied extensi…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The radical pair mechanism is a quantum-mechanical process underlying weak magnetic field effects in chemical and biological systems. While nuclear polarization and electronic entanglement in this mechanism have been studied extensively, the possibility of creating entanglement between nuclear spins has, to the best of our knowledge, remained unexplored. Here, we show that nuclear-spin entanglement can develop from initially maximally mixed nuclear spin states and evolve over repeated radical pair cycles. Its generation and persistence depend on the initial electronic state, the available reaction channels, and the interplay between recombination rates, hyperfine interactions, and the magnetic field. We demonstrate this behaviour in both a minimal two-nucleus model and a five-nucleus model inspired by the photosynthetic radical pair P700--$A_1$. Radical pair mechanism generated nuclear-spin entanglement offers a potential new resource for quantum technologies and opens avenues for exploring its role in biological systems.

item.title: Finite-time spectral enhancement of transient quantum thermometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.17522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transient quantum thermometry extracts temperature information before a probe reaches thermal equilibrium. We study how finite interaction times affect thermometric precision for a harmonic-oscillator probe prepared in a number stat…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transient quantum thermometry extracts temperature information before a probe reaches thermal equilibrium. We study how finite interaction times affect thermometric precision for a harmonic-oscillator probe prepared in a number state and weakly coupled to a thermal bosonic reservoir. A second-order time-convolutionless master equation retains the finite-time reservoir response, allowing modes away from the probe frequency to shape the populations and their temperature dependence. For the baseline parameters, this response raises the quantum Fisher information about fivefold above the Markovian prediction, in agreement with an exact solution of the model. When the probability of leaving the initial state is small, we derive an analytical condition for this enhancement. To assess its operational significance, we examine the temperature information acquired per unit time. Under the exact dynamics, this rate is largest within the reservoir memory time. With negligible preparation and readout overhead, the optimum is about five times the best Markovian rate and 30 times an upper bound on the equilibrium rate. The advantage survives smooth switching, although overhead and longer coupling ramps reduce it.

item.title: Recursive Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz
item.description: arXiv:2611.17537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recursive quantum approximate optimisation algorithm~(RQAOA) shrinks an unconstrained combinatorial optimisation problem by eliminating one variable at a time, guided by correlations measured in variational quantum states. We ex…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recursive quantum approximate optimisation algorithm~(RQAOA) shrinks an unconstrained combinatorial optimisation problem by eliminating one variable at a time, guided by correlations measured in variational quantum states. We extend this recursion to constrained problems by building on the quantum alternating operator ansatz, which restricts the evolution to feasible solutions through a feasible initial state and feasibility-preserving mixers. However, every elimination alters the feasibility structure, so that such a mixer for the original problem generally fails to be one for the subproblems. Previous extensions to Maximum Independent Set and Minimum Vertex Cover sidestep this with tailored reduction rules that keep every subproblem within the original problem class. We resolve this by identifying, for a given constraint structure, a broader problem class that is closed under all eliminations, and by efficiently constructing feasible initial states and feasibility-preserving mixers for every class member. We do so for monotone constraints, such as for the knapsack problem, for linear equality constraints with polynomially bounded weights, including Hamming weight constraints, and for combinations of equality constraints with a single inequality constraint, such as the cardinality-constrained knapsack problem. Conversely, we show that these restrictions cannot be lifted in general without leaving the realm of efficient constructions. Exact simulations on knapsack and vertex-weighted max-bisection instances demonstrate that our recursive scheme can outperform both its non-recursive counterpart and penalty-based QAOA and RQAOA.

item.title: DRAG-Inspired Single Flux Quantum Control of Superconducting Qubits
item.description: arXiv:2611.17562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalable control remains a major challenge for superconducting quantum processors due to the wiring, thermal load, and hardware complexity associated with conventional microwave-based architectures. A framework for qubit control bas…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalable control remains a major challenge for superconducting quantum processors due to the wiring, thermal load, and hardware complexity associated with conventional microwave-based architectures. A framework for qubit control based on Single Flux Quantum (SFQ) digital electronics is presented. For transmon qubits, optimized control sequences are constructed from regular pulse trains framed by arbitrary subsequences (ramps), enabling DRAG-inspired leakage suppression in the discrete SFQ regime through genetic-algorithm optimization. For representative $Y_{\pi/2}$ gates, the resulting sequences achieve simulated coherent-control infidelities below $10^{-4}$, including leakage from the computational subspace. The objective of the proposed approach is to demonstrate that coherent errors intrinsic to SFQ control can be reduced to a comparable level for a more scalable cryogenic control architecture. Memory requirements are reduced by storing only the optimized ramps, while a modular controller architecture supporting both regular and arbitrary pulse generation is proposed. The logical complexity of this architecture is estimated from the Josephson-junction counts of its constituent SFQ cells. The proposed approach therefore combines low coherent-control error with reduced memory overhead and provides a basis for scalable cryogenic SFQ control architectures.

item.title: Magic of Dicke states: density, cost and yield
item.description: arXiv:2611.17623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of $L$ qubits with $n$ excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of $L$ qubits with $n$ excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE), is extensive at every filling $f=n/L$ except half-filling, and we obtain the magic density analytically, together with the subleading terms. In the context of fault-tolerant quantum computation, we also investigate the yield of Dicke states, and find that they can produce on average an extensive number of CCZ states (or $T$ states with a catalyst) at any $0<1$. This yield is not self-averaging, but fluctuates from run to run by $O(L)$, as if it were set by a hidden phase shared by all qubits. At half-filling, the SRE grows only logarithmically, while the preparation cost, average yield and relative entropy of magic remain extensive, so that a small SRE does not necessarily signal a weak resource. These results can be understood by viewing the Dicke state as a fixed-magnetization projection of a product of tilted spins.

item.title: Linear monitoring-feedback Model for Linearized gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.17642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical gravity and, when quantum resources are supplied in correlated ancilla inputs, can reproduce linearized quantum-gravity dynamics. Auxiliary systems monitor the positions of massive bodies, and their records are fed back through a chosen gravitational response kernel. At the level of linear input-output theory, this construction makes the deterministic response explicit while exposing the force noise and correlations associated with the auxiliary sector. We organize the allowed ancilla correlations into three regimes. In Regime-I, independent ancillas have unsqueezed, uncorrelated sensing and back-action quadratures. A single object then has a minimum classical-gravity noise (CGN), S_F^min = 2 hbar M Omega_SN^2, where Omega_SN is the Schrodinger-Newton frequency set by the microscopic mass distribution. In Regime-II, arbitrary local sensing--back-action correlations are allowed, but the ancillas associated with different objects remain independent. The single-object CGN is then unrestricted, while the joint force-noise matrix obeys a determinant bound that is equivalent to the local classical-channel/no-entanglement bound. In Regime-III, cross-object correlations and a common nonlocal mediator are allowed. The commuting force noises can then be jointly squeezed, entanglement between the masses can occur, and--with a suitable retarded response and input state--the monitoring-feedback system can reproduce the noise and commutators of linearized quantum gravity, including non-Markovian quantum fluctuations.

item.title: Quantum Data Processing Unit for Neutral-Atom Quantum Computers
item.description: arXiv:2611.17652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computers need real-time classical processing to convert measurement data into feedback within device-specific timing constraints. We introduce the quantum data processing unit (QDPU), an architecture between a quantum devic…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computers need real-time classical processing to convert measurement data into feedback within device-specific timing constraints. We introduce the quantum data processing unit (QDPU), an architecture between a quantum device and its controller. Its core is a machine-learned quantum data model (QDM), adapted to the measurement response and noise characteristics of the device. We implement an FPGA pipeline for neutral-atom array assembly that performs occupancy detection and rearrangement scheduling in FPGA logic. One calibrated matched-filter lane classifies a $50\times50$ array in 12.5 $\mu$s. An atom-loss model using a software reference planner evaluates a $35\times35$ target with a 60 s trap lifetime and 0.1% loss per moved atom. Removing an assumed 150 ms host round trip raises the predicted assembly success from 8% to 85% and reduces the wall-clock time per successful assembly from 19 s to 0.16 s. A GPU-based outer loop is proposed for refitting model parameters between runs. Its NVQLink transport is measured on the board: over 10 GbE to an NVIDIA DGX Spark, the median FPGA-to-host-to-FPGA round trip is 2.74 $\mu$s for 128-byte messages forwarded by a CPU core. A separate 12-bit learned qLDPC kernel is placed and routed for the same FPGA target, with a derived latency of 0.84 ms per round for a $[[1122,148]]$ lifted-product code under code-capacity noise. A quantised GraphMP ranking kernel for the same code runs on the board with a median host-to-FPGA-to-host latency of 50.5 $\mu$s with one shot in flight, excluding host-side BP+OSD post-processing. Together, these implementations illustrate a shared architecture with workload-specific models and timing requirements.

item.title: Fast forward-and-backward creation of non-equilibrium Gibbs state in driven dissipative quantum systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.17738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the fast-forward (FF) approach to adiabatic time evolution of an open dissipative quantum system within the framework of the Gorini-Kosaakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) equation. Taking a harmonic oscillator (HO) and a q…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the fast-forward (FF) approach to adiabatic time evolution of an open dissipative quantum system within the framework of the Gorini-Kosaakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) equation. Taking a harmonic oscillator (HO) and a quantum spin as prototype systems under a rapid change of the driving field and in contact with the heat reservoir, we reveal the protocol which creates the non-equilibrium Gibbs state. After preparing the Gibbs state under the fixed external field in advance, we begin to change adiabatically the field. To keep a quasi-adiabatic version of the Gibbs state as the solution of GKSL equation, we solve the inverse problem to obtain the non-adiabatic corrections both to Hamiltonian and to the dissipator. Then we apply the fast forward-and-backward (abbreviated as FF for convenience) time-rescaling, obtaining the FF variants of both Hamiltonian and detailed balance condition (DBC) among dissipative coefficients. The present scheme generates the time-periodic Gibbs state as if a limit-cycle solution of the innovated GKSL equation under the time-periodic driving field. Thanks to the FF variant of DBC, we see the energy conservation of power and heat current of the system, and reversibility of whole system including a reservoir. The requirement of positivity of the FF dissipative coefficients imposes a constraint on the speed of the FF driving. At low temperature, the upper speed limit of the FF periodic driving is found to be proportional to $\tilde{\beta}^{-1/2}\exp(a\tilde{\beta})$ with $\tilde{\beta}$ the scaled inverse temperature and $a$ the positive constant of $O(1)$.

item.title: Multitime Equilibration and Multitime Mpemba Effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.17749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Equilibration of a quantum state leaves open whether its response to later interventions has also equilibrated. We establish multitime equilibration for a continuous process on a fixed observation window, retaining the autonomous sy…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Equilibration of a quantum state leaves open whether its response to later interventions has also equilibrated. We establish multitime equilibration for a continuous process on a fixed observation window, retaining the autonomous system--environment dynamics and all internal time differences. A finite-time mean-square bound controls the full continuous-process norm through the effective energy dimension and energy-gap correlations. A factorial temporal-order bound lifts fixed-sector convergence to the full process, while a process-visible spectral measure distinguishes mean-square from pointwise equilibration. This framework defines multitime Mpemba effects by comparing preparations relative to one stationary process. In a semicircle-spectrum model, a preparation filter changes the decay exponent from $3/2$ to $5/2$ in every fixed sector and in the summed norm, despite a larger initial distance. A fixed unitary control and terminal measurement exhibit the same exponent improvement in their output probabilities. Noncommuting baths and a many-body spin environment separate this all-sector mechanism from selective finite-time acceleration.

item.title: Tight Quantum Query Bounds for Collision Finding over Arbitrary Bounded Types
item.description: arXiv:2611.17804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the bounded-error quantum query complexity of finding one $r$-collision in an $N$-input function of prescribed type, which specifies all equality-class sizes. For every fixed maximum class size and collision order, we g…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the bounded-error quantum query complexity of finding one $r$-collision in an $N$-input function of prescribed type, which specifies all equality-class sizes. For every fixed maximum class size and collision order, we give a tight bound as the maximum of scales determined by the numbers of classes of size at least $2,\ldots,r$. The lower bound holds for a uniformly random function of that type, and a matching algorithm succeeds on every such function. No intermediate class size is required to occur, and every feasible output alphabet is allowed. The characterization connects the abundant-collision regime associated with set equality to the sparse-target regime of $k$-distinctness. In particular, finding the unique $(k+1)$-collision in type $(k^n,k+1)$ has complexity $\Theta_k(N^{3/4-1/[4(2^{k+1}-1)]})$, where $N=kn+k+1$, resolving an open problem of Belovs. For the lower bound, we introduce a filtered compressed permutation oracle that projects onto a harmonic database subspace after each complete function query. Its $O(T/N)$ comparison error over $T$ queries overcomes the square-root limitation of the unfiltered process. Hidden capacity extensions and moment estimates retain the populations at each intermediate collision order. Matching upper bounds use sampled collision lists and colored adaptive learning graphs, with a coherent decision-to-search conversion that avoids logarithmic overhead. We also give an alternative nested quantum-walk algorithm for three-collision search, matching the bound up to polylogarithmic factors.

item.title: No universal LOCC entanglement purification
item.description: arXiv:2611.17809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement purification aims to obtain high-fidelity entangled states from noisy entangled states. This task becomes particularly challenging when the available input states are finite in number, only partially characterized, and …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement purification aims to obtain high-fidelity entangled states from noisy entangled states. This task becomes particularly challenging when the available input states are finite in number, only partially characterized, and may not be identical. Whether there exists a universal purification protocol applicable to such inputs has therefore been a longstanding question. This motivates the study of universal $n$-to-$1$ entanglement purification. Although no such LOCC protocol exists for the full set of two-qubit entangled states, it has remained open whether this no-go result extends to higher-dimensional bipartite states and multipartite states. In this work, we resolve this question by proving that, for any fixed finite local dimensions, no $n$-to-$1$ LOCC protocol is universal for all bipartite entangled states or all multipartite entangled states. We further show that the bipartite and multipartite no-go results persist under several natural extensions and establish an analogous no-go theorem for coherence purification under strictly incoherent operations.

item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a charge-$4e$ parafermionic-vortex route to qutrit processing as a conditional theory with explicit operational assumptions. Sector preservation and same-label charge-conjugation covariance imply closure for every adaptive visible record. For charge-conjugation-invariant inputs, record probabilities are independent of the supported reference state; for arbitrary inputs, discarding the reference gives a population-weighted mixture of conjugate sector maps. We give a finite-depth stability bound for complete labelled instruments, including postselection and initial zero-sector contamination. A self-contained calculation reproduces the known dense single-qutrit closure of the registered Clifford-plus-Flip gate set. We also specify an abstract ternary CSS $[[11,1,5]]_3$ syndrome/recovery decoder: 243 classical representatives per CSS component correct all 3,609 Pauli errors of support weight at most two, and an exact integer dynamic program yields the full independent-Pauli logical enumerator. Its all-syndrome acceptance is distinct from the known $1/1728$ ideal acceptance of one-round strange-state Golay distillation. An accepted-run target-infidelity budget and a synthetic parameter protocol expose the remaining noise assumptions. Native charge-$4e$ syndrome extraction, material feasibility, a device threshold, and unconditional fault tolerance are not established.

item.title: Four-Sector Propagation-Trapping Decomposition and Inverse Design of Initial States in Grover-Coined Quantum Walks on Multiedge Path Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.17837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling propagation and trapping through initial-state preparation requires an explicit relation between the initial amplitudes and the corresponding directional probabilities. We establish this relation for a discrete-time Grov…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling propagation and trapping through initial-state preparation requires an explicit relation between the initial amplitudes and the corresponding directional probabilities. We establish this relation for a discrete-time Grover-coined quantum walk on a multiedge path graph with even degree d = 2M, where M is at least 2, and two equal directional blocks. Each block of an arbitrary local state is expressed as its mean component plus a zero-sum deviation. The Grover coin performs a pure exchange of the two block means and reverses the sign of each zero-sum deviation. Together with the graph routing, this gives a unique orthogonal decomposition into four sectors: propagation in opposite directions and bounded trapping on either side of the launch vertex. We derive the four sector probabilities and solve the inverse problem, constructing initial states for any prescribed nonnegative probability quadruple that sums to unity. Explicit representatives are given for d = 4 and d = 6. Sector-resolved simulations reproduce the predicted motion, conservation of sector weights, and local probability additivity, including repeated spatial overlaps. We also derive the local Grover action for an arbitrary partition into blocks of possibly unequal sizes, explicitly describing how their means are redistributed while each zero-sum deviation remains within its block and changes sign. The framework provides direct control of propagation and trapping within one fixed graph and walk operator through the preparation of the initial state.

item.title: Hardware-aware sampling and QPU-informed Monte Carlo with quantum annealers
item.description: arXiv:2611.17842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how the physical representation of a logical model affects sampling by quantum annealers and its use in corrected Monte Carlo. The square-lattice Ising model provides controlled classical references. Fixed embeddings with o…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how the physical representation of a logical model affects sampling by quantum annealers and its use in corrected Monte Carlo. The square-lattice Ising model provides controlled classical references. Fixed embeddings with one physical qubit per logical spin reach $36\times36$ spins. Comparisons with uniform two-qubit chains and mixed chain lengths show that matching mean energy leaves differences in magnetization and correlations. Extended-range conditional predictors improve the description of mixed embeddings, distinguishing their residual correlations from those of the tested uniform embeddings. Independent calibration checks and fixed-scale annealing scans show that temperature shifts alone do not determine distributional agreement. Normalized autoregressive models learned from QPU samples provide proposals with exact Metropolis--Hastings and multiple-try corrections on larger periodic lattices. These preserve the target distribution, although block updates alone relax critical magnetization slowly. Complementary direct-QPU updates reveal how block size and fitted-temperature correction affect acceptance and spin motion. Together, the results support prioritizing one-qubit representations and short uniform chains, while separating hardware sampling fidelity from the convergence of corrected Monte Carlo.

item.title: Underlying orbital U(1) symmetry in quantum limit cycles
item.description: arXiv:2611.17890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum limit cycles exhibit harmonic Liouvillian spectra, yet their underlying orbital $U(1)$ structure is not generally explicit in the absence of physical rotational symmetry. Here, we construct a unitary representation of orbita…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum limit cycles exhibit harmonic Liouvillian spectra, yet their underlying orbital $U(1)$ structure is not generally explicit in the absence of physical rotational symmetry. Here, we construct a unitary representation of orbital phase translations through a similarity transformation that maps the harmonic nondecaying Liouvillian sector onto a Hermitian angular-momentum Hamiltonian. The resulting phase states possess homogeneous Fubini--Study geometry independently of the physical orbit's shape. For ideal quantum limit cycles, the corresponding density matrix also exhibit homogeneous Bures geometry. At finite size, we show how phase diffusion damps slow Liouvillian harmonics while preserving the effective orbital $U(1)$ symmetry. The resulting loss of phase-state distinguishability and contraction of the effective geometry are quantitatively predicted by the microscopic slow Liouvillian spectrum. Our results establish a connection between orbital phase symmetry, quantum geometry, and finite-size phase diffusion in open quantum systems.

item.title: Hybrid Uncertainty in the Real Forms of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.17896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An optimized commutator bound can lie strictly below the quantum infimum even when its minimizing mean is realized by a quantum state. We study hybrid uncertainty, defined as the sum of pairwise products of standard deviations. For …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An optimized commutator bound can lie strictly below the quantum infimum even when its minimizing mean is realized by a quantum state. We study hybrid uncertainty, defined as the sum of pairwise products of standard deviations. For any spanning list of nonzero real linear combinations of the generators in a positive discrete series representation of $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$, the commutator bound has a unique minimizing mean, realized by a Perelomov coherent state. We prove that the optimized bound equals the infimum over states with finite second moments if and only if the symmetrized covariance matrix of the prescribed observables is diagonal in this state. When this condition fails, the quantum infimum is strictly greater than the bound; for a nonorthogonal list, we obtain an explicit positive lower bound on this gap. For irreducible spin-$j$ representations of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, we derive the exact minimum of the spectral hybrid uncertainty over states for any spanning list of spin observables. For a fixed state, we compare separate measurements made before a random target is disclosed with direct measurement of the target known in advance. For these protocols, the excess mean squared error coefficient equals twice the listed hybrid uncertainty, and its minimum over orthogonal combinations of the observables equals twice the spectral hybrid uncertainty.

item.description: arXiv:2611.17906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum switch (QS) interferometer within a Bohmian framework and show how the notion of causality is preserved in this approach. Furthermore, we investigate device-independent certification and causal inequalities applied to an entangled quantum system, and show that in this regime too, the notions of trajectories and of a strict causal order are perfectly preserved.

item.title: Data re-uploading in Quantum Reservoir Computing
item.description: arXiv:2611.17913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data re-uploading enhances the learnable function space of parameterized quantum circuits and has become standard practice in circuit-based \ac{qml}. Its role in quantum reservoir computing, however, remains largely unexplored. Here…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data re-uploading enhances the learnable function space of parameterized quantum circuits and has become standard practice in circuit-based \ac{qml}. Its role in quantum reservoir computing, however, remains largely unexplored. Here, we introduce data re-uploading into physical quantum reservoir computing and show that repeated input encoding significantly enhances the learnability of higher-order nonlinear polynomials and improves performance on chaotic time-series prediction tasks. We consider protocols with either fixed or increasing computational cost and compare them with a complementary dissipative protocol to distinguish the effects of repeated input encoding from those of additional state overwriting. Using the information processing capacity framework, we identify a memory--nonlinearity trade-off: increasing the number of encodings shifts capacity toward higher-order nonlinearities. In contrast, the dissipative protocol does not extend the range of learnable nonlinear orders and yields only limited improvements in task performance. These results establish data re-uploading as an effective means of tuning and enhancing nonlinear processing in physical quantum reservoir computing.

item.title: Dissipation-induced integrability in a spin-1 chain and a Bose-Hubbard mixture
item.description: arXiv:2611.17928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a nonintegrable spin-1 chain that acquires a Yang--Baxter integrable no-jump Hamiltonian through a single dissipative channel per bond. Energy is the only nontrivial finite-range charge of the isolated periodic bulk. In…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a nonintegrable spin-1 chain that acquires a Yang--Baxter integrable no-jump Hamiltonian through a single dissipative channel per bond. Energy is the only nontrivial finite-range charge of the isolated periodic bulk. Interference cancels the reverse spin conversions, leaving directed moves that obey nil-Coxeter relations and generate commuting charges of increasing range on the open chain. We obtain the full Liouvillian spectrum at any chain length and identify an exponentially large set of blocked spin configurations whose superpositions are all stationary. Resolving the bond outputs leaves the no-jump Hamiltonian unchanged; each bond on which two configurations differ then contributes equally to their dephasing. In a two-component Bose--Hubbard chain, opposite loss phases produce counterpropagating species whose motion and collisions enter a common transfer matrix when interspecies attraction matches intraspecies repulsion. At this coupling, redistributing a pair costs no interaction energy in the atomic limit. Such bond interference offers a route to integrability in other open quantum many-body systems.

item.title: Efficient representations by PEPS: critical free-fermion and chiral topological states
item.description: arXiv:2611.17936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct projected entangled-pair state (PEPS) approximations to various many-body states in 2D lattices with global error at most $\epsilon$ and bond dimension polynomial in the system size and $1/\epsilon$. They include critic…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct projected entangled-pair state (PEPS) approximations to various many-body states in 2D lattices with global error at most $\epsilon$ and bond dimension polynomial in the system size and $1/\epsilon$. They include critical free-fermion models in two dimensions, as well as chiral topological states. For the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor tight-binding model at half filling, our construction combines Gaussian wavelet transformations with matrix product state approximations of the one-dimensional chains, as well as selected fermionic swap operations. For arbitrary uniformly gapped, finite-range quadratic Hamiltonians, we give a different construction based on repeated one-particle filtering, which yields Gaussian PEPS in any spatial dimension. Those include, for instance, $p+ip$ models or a Chern-insulator in a square lattice, for which we give an explicit construction. Finally, we prove that Gutzwiller projections of a fixed number of identical Gaussian PEPS approximations to free-fermion states at arbitrary filling do not amplify considerably the approximation error. This provides a polynomial-bond PEPS approximations to the resulting states, including familiar lattice chiral-spin-liquid states.

item.title: Benchmarking superconducting quantum processors with percolating entanglement quality
item.description: arXiv:2611.17941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The capability to create large entanglement resources is a key performance attribute of quantum processors, and the size of the resource is often used as a benchmark of processor scale. Recent graph-state experiments have reported e…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The capability to create large entanglement resources is a key performance attribute of quantum processors, and the size of the resource is often used as a benchmark of processor scale. Recent graph-state experiments have reported entanglement clusters spanning entire chips with hundreds of qubits. However, cluster size alone does not capture the entanglement quality of individual couplings or differences in coupling topology. Here, we introduce percolating entanglement quality (PEQ), a topology-normalized benchmark based on conditional two-qubit negativity and a topology-specific bond-percolation threshold. As an experimental demonstration, we prepare a native graph state on a 64-qubit square-lattice superconducting processor with defects, identify a 52-qubit entanglement cluster, and evaluate the PEQ of the processor. Applying PEQ to previously reported chip-wide graph-state measurements on heavy-hex-lattice processors, we show that PEQ differs substantially among processors whose entanglement clusters span the entire chip. PEQ provides a single chip-wide score without selecting a best-performing qubit subset or path. This score allows processors with different coupling topologies to be compared on a common scale and can inform the design of coupling topologies for scalable chips.

item.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
item.description: arXiv:2611.17948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound. However, local algebras…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace and normal states have no density matrices, so the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.

item.title: Digital Coherent Twin-Field Quantum Key Distribution with Gaussian-Modulated Coherent States
item.description: arXiv:2611.17970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables information-theoretically secure key sharing between two distant parties. Recently, one promising QKD protocol which can distribute a secret key over long distances called twin-field QKD (TF-QK…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables information-theoretically secure key sharing between two distant parties. Recently, one promising QKD protocol which can distribute a secret key over long distances called twin-field QKD (TF-QKD) has been developed. However, it requires active compensation for experimental imperfections such as phase, polarization, and frequency fluctuations with expensive devices and this makes its experimental implementation challenging. Here, we propose a long-distance continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD) protocol which is inspired by TF-QKD. Our protocol can remove these requirements by using Gaussian-modulated coherent states and digital signal processing which is widely used in recent digital coherent optical communication and experimental implementations of CV-QKD. For security analysis, we use a numerical optimization approach with a photon-number cutoff assumption. We propose a new set of constraints for numerical optimization which can efficiently constrain a highly non-Gaussian quantum state shared by two legitimate parties in our protocol. We show that the key rate of our protocol exceeds the key rate of a direct-transmission CV-QKD protocol at long distances and it can overcome the repeaterless bound.

item.title: A Concise Introduction to Quantum Electromagnetics
item.description: arXiv:2611.17988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This book introduces quantum electromagnetics to readers trained in classical electromagnetics, without assuming a systematic background in quantum mechanics. The central question is when classical descriptions suffice, and when the…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.17988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This book introduces quantum electromagnetics to readers trained in classical electromagnetics, without assuming a systematic background in quantum mechanics. The central question is when classical descriptions suffice, and when the quantum states of matter or the field must be retained explicitly. Starting from familiar electromagnetic modes and material response, the discussion develops atomic dynamics, field quantization, and the interaction of quantized fields with quantum matter. Particular attention is given to how mode profiles, Green functions, and scattering matrices obtained from classical electromagnetic calculations enter quantum models. Atomic coherence, photon statistics, spontaneous emission, and cavity coupling are developed through derivations that identify the physical assumptions and limits of each description. Examples drawn from atomic clocks, Rydberg-atom receivers, and single-photon devices connect these concepts to excitation, propagation, and measurement in practical systems. Loss and noise are included in relating internal dynamics to measured signals and correlations. The final discussion examines how sensitivity and claims of quantum advantage depend on bandwidth, measurement resources, and the classical reference used for comparison. The aim is to help readers choose an appropriate model, carry out the calculation, and understand what its predictions mean for an electromagnetic measurement.

item.title: The cone of states over time: exact tests and convergent two-sided hierarchies
item.description: arXiv:2611.18001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A state over time (stote) pairs a state $\rho$ with a channel $\mathcal{E}$ as the Hermitian, generally non-positive operator $(\rho\otimes\mathbf{1})\star J_\mathcal{E}$. We study the convex cone $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$ generated b…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.18001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A state over time (stote) pairs a state $\rho$ with a channel $\mathcal{E}$ as the Hermitian, generally non-positive operator $(\rho\otimes\mathbf{1})\star J_\mathcal{E}$. We study the convex cone $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$ generated by these operators. Our main result is a convergent outer semidefinite hierarchy with an explicit trace-norm Hausdorff bound on its trace-one slices. Specializing constrained symmetric-extension theory to the input--channel representation, we show that Bose-extension rounding preserves the channel marginal constraint and gives error at most $2d_A^2(d_A-1)/(k+d_A-1)$ at level $k$. A complementary inner hierarchy retains all channels at each chosen pure-input direction. For $d_A\ge2$, its error is at most $2(d_A-1)\sin^2\delta$, where $\delta$ is the Fubini--Study covering radius; nested sets of $N$ directions give error at most $2\pi^2(d_A-1)N^{-1/(d_A-1)}$, independently of $d_B$. These bounds provide explicit size--accuracy guarantees and certified support-value bounds, without guaranteeing finite termination for exact boundary membership. For binary classical outputs, we obtain an exact SDP membership test, including indefinite output blocks and mixtures that are not single stotes. At faithful marginal the test reduces to a scalar inequality; every trace-one member of this sector with input marginal $\rho$ has a constructive realization using at most $\operatorname{rank}\rho$ pure-input stotes with binary measurement channels. Finally, we compute the exact isotropic boundary and prove $\mathrm{PPT}\subsetneq\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\cap\mathrm{PSD}\subsetneq\mathrm{PSD}$ for equal local dimensions at least two.

item.title: Max-Cut QAOA on Non-Hardware-Native Graphs via MinLA Surrogates and Configuration Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2611.18002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For non-hardware-native \textsc{MAX-CUT} instances, the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can incur additional two-qubit depth overhead due to SWAP-based routing of interactions between non-adjacent qubits. We propos…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.18002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For non-hardware-native \textsc{MAX-CUT} instances, the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can incur additional two-qubit depth overhead due to SWAP-based routing of interactions between non-adjacent qubits. We propose a hybrid quantum--classical workflow that reduces this depth by selectively removing interactions and subsequently recovers solution quality through classical optimization of the original \textsc{MAX-CUT} objective. We employ a Minimum Linear Arrangement (MinLA)-based vertex ordering to preferentially retain short-range interactions, thereby constructing a two-qubit depth-reduced surrogate QAOA ansatz. To compensate for the information lost through interaction removal, we develop classical \textit{recovery} strategies that refine QPU-sampled bitstrings directly on the original \textsc{MAX-CUT} objective. We develop two recovery strategies: signed-residue-based local search and bipartite-block optimization, where each conditional block problem is solved exactly using an $s$--$t$ minimum cut. Recovery is performed independently on each sampled configuration, ensuring monotonic improvement in cut value without additional QPU executions. We evaluate the workflow on \texttt{ibm\_kingston} for 120 distinct non-hardware-native instances comprising $6$-regular and Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs with 40, 60 and 100 vertices. We verify that the surrogates substantially reduce transpiled two-qubit depth while staying within the prescribed two-qubit depth, and with recovery yield \textit{near-optimal} cuts on the original graphs. These results demonstrate the potential of hardware-aware interaction selection and classical recovery to extend QAOA to graph instances whose full cost Hamiltonians exceed practical circuit-depth budgets.

item.title: Quantum kinetic uncertainty relations: Role of coherence in current fluctuation bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.18037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comparative analysis of three quantum versions of the kinetic uncertainty relation (KUR), which incorporate coherence-dependent corrections to the classical bound. Using a three-level maser heat engine as a paradigmatic…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.18037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comparative analysis of three quantum versions of the kinetic uncertainty relation (KUR), which incorporate coherence-dependent corrections to the classical bound. Using a three-level maser heat engine as a paradigmatic quantum thermal machine, we identify the operating regimes in which each formulation provides the tightest constraint on current fluctuations. We further identify tighter, model-specific bounds for two of these formulations, provide numerical support for both, and establish one of them analytically. Introducing ground-state degeneracy, we then demonstrate that noise-induced coherence provides a tunable resource for relocating, enhancing, or suppressing violations of the standard KUR without requiring an additional coherent drive. In particular, it enables violations in regimes where the three-level engine satisfies the classical bound. Our results clarify how distinct quantum KURs account for coherence and constrain the precision of quantum thermal machines.

item.title: Hidden Quantum Markov Processes: Mealy Formulation and Observable Reduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.18040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate hidden quantum Markov processes in a Mealy architecture using a single completely positive unital transition expectation coupling the present hidden system, the emitted output, and the next hidden system. Together with …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.18040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate hidden quantum Markov processes in a Mealy architecture using a single completely positive unital transition expectation coupling the present hidden system, the emitted output, and the next hidden system. Together with a boundary state, it generates a quasi-local, finitely correlated hidden--output state; for the commutative generator associated with a classical Mealy kernel, this state is the full joint law of the classical Mealy model. Moore realizations correspond to transition expectations that factor on the prescribed hidden algebra. We establish a rank obstruction to such factorization and prove its sufficiency for isometric generators: factorization holds exactly when the induced hidden-memory channel has Kraus rank at most the hidden Hilbert-space dimension. The Kraus rank also gives the minimal intermediate Hilbert-space dimension. When the hidden and output dimensions are at least two, the factorizable isometric generators form a closed subset of measure zero. For any fixed projective readout, a Mealy generator induces an operational hidden quantum Markov model in the sense of Monr\`as, Beige and Wiesner; conversely, every finite-dimensional operational model admits a Mealy lift on the same memory space with a rank-one readout. For their cluster-state instrument, two isometric, Moore-factorizable lifts with the same instrument and initial memory state yield identical measured output statistics but different quantum output states: one has marginals entangled across $1|2\cdots n$ for $n\geq3$, with three-output negativity $\tfrac12$, whereas the other has fully separable marginals. Thus operational equivalence does not determine output entanglement.
